findings.summary: Wave-3 integration defect found in the coordinator's browser pass: WP-15.3 (accepted) added qualification.wall_time_seconds to the provider-availability DTO, and the strict client parser (hasExactKeys on the qualification block in frontend/work/src/api.ts) rejected the additive key, so every provider-availability read failed: the Tasks view showed request_unavailable and Settings said availability could not be read. Fixed by the coordinator: the client accepts the optional key (integer 30..1800 or null; absent = not provided), exposes qualification.wallTimeSeconds, with a DTO-shape test. Lesson: an 'additive' server field is only additive once the client's exact-key parser admits it; backend packages that extend a DTO need the client half in the same wave.

Projection fixed-point strips a superseded acceptance non-causally and collapses valid history. Reproduction: task.3XJNY0AR6Q3PMDM9AERRYWQQ4K held July chain submit(evt.01KY9S721J) -> accepted(evt.01KYA18SEF) -> reopened(evt.01KYA5Q3KX) -> submitted(evt.01KYA6HZ1R). Recording a new acceptance today (evt.01M07MF21T, since invalidated as the repair) made replay strip the July acceptance because its bound review is stale at end-of-history, reject the already-applied reopen as stale-expected, truncate the chain, drop the fresh review.58W4H4P31H4PYEQRQD6EF8T769, and turn doctor red blocking unrelated writes. The guard must evaluate causally: an acceptance superseded by a later reopen is history, not a live claim. Doctor green again after invalidating the trigger. Until fixed, accepting any task with an acceptance-then-reopen history re-triggers the collapse; task.3XJNY0AR6Q3PMDM9AERRYWQQ4K cannot be accepted safely.

Heterogeneous provider launch has two independent availability failures that static preflight cannot represent: Claude can be signed out or unable to persist provider-owned credentials, while nested Codex initialization can be blocked by the outer execution-host sandbox. Product remediation requires separate typed auth/host/init/canary states, async provider-owned auth recovery, no child/attempt on pure pre-start refusal, and an operator-owned authenticated broker host for reciprocal nested launches. Retry, credential copying and silent fallback are unsafe.

Repository documentation had conflicting current/withdrawn/shipped claims and no single routing page; cleanup added an explicit authority map, corrected stale operational and setup references, and aligned Starter Pack status with the current read-only implementation.

CentOS 9 L1 live qualification exposed a Grok builder control-plane bypass: the real Grok builder process can finish canonical delegation state without an audited worker-MCP terminal outcome when native run_terminal_cmd can reach the Agent Commons CLI with broker child bindings. The observed signature was canonical_state=succeeded with terminal_tool_calls=0; reviewer, which lacked native shell, failed closed. Remediation task task.6XC7JQJMS5CFMWD1M0V3885DXA removes Grok builder native shell and strips Agent Commons control-plane env from Grok native shell policy; L1 still requires a fresh CentOS live rerun on the remediation commit.

P2 unresolved first-open concurrency failure in immutable Git commit 405d8c690d3c7e33fedb63828db9d30e6a6185e9, src/agent_commons/runtime/message_delivery.py:103: os.open of receipts.lock with O_CREAT can raise ENOENT under four synchronized first-open workers. Lead-reported stronger evidence: full make check failed one test with 2585 passed and 13 skipped; independent outside-pytest reproduction failed at cycle 3 in 0.97 seconds with the existing linked root retaining the same device/inode and no root unlink. This establishes first attachment-delivery availability risk, not proven loss of confirmed updates. The earlier R5 approved review review.50FYAXT2W7MPAV7RF9V2FCD9B6 at evt.01M21GTYCEY6Q2E005HRZCH8PD is a historical judgment contradicted by this later reproduction and must not support acceptance. R6 review remains paused; R5 and R6 require corrected successor source, gates and independent review. Reporter independently reviewed original source/tests but did not execute this later reproduction; reproduction attribution remains explicit.

Task 1 pre-CAS stale-acceptance guard counts unapplied successors. Repro at main@0107fc8: after an approved review is non-structurally corrected, add two task.reopened events that both name the live task.accepted event as expected_revision. _cas_conflicts rejects both successors, yet _stale_task_acceptance_ids builds built_upon from all materialized events, so it does not strip the live acceptance; projection remains state=accepted, acceptance_stale=false, review effective revision moves, and fixed_point_passes=1. This violates the Batch 0 live-tail guarantee and the task's causal applied-event requirement. Compute the pre-CAS exemption from successors proven effective, or otherwise ensure rejected/conflicted successors cannot shield a live acceptance, and add this regression.

Task 2's Node-stdin law is false as written. AGENTS.md says scripts fed to node must travel over stdin, and docs/FRONTEND_CONTRACT.md says Node harness scripts travel over stdin. But tests/ui/test_board_order_and_units_guide.py:112-113 invokes subprocess.run(["node", "-e", harness, ...]), passing the JavaScript program as an argv element. The large STRINGS harness correctly uses node '-' plus input=, but the contract is universal. Either move the layout harness to stdin or narrow both documents to the size-sensitive STRINGS harness; add a check if the universal rule is intended.

Delegated codex children have no agent-commons MCP wiring: CodexRunnerProfile.build_invocation (runtime/model.py) passes no MCP config to the codex CLI, so a codex child can never call commons_succeed_delegation or any terminal tool. Every codex delegation therefore ends needs_operator (terminal_tool_not_called) even when the work fully succeeds. Evidence 2026-07-23, external pilot workspace pilot-site: delegation.7P7A7Z0T7KD2YA6TVQE5PY41ET (codex-builder, purpose implementation) produced a correct backend (4/4 tests parent-verified, later independently approved) yet finalized needs_operator/invalid_result with terminal_tool_calls:0. Codex CLI 0.144+ supports -c mcp_servers.* overrides in exec, so wiring the generated MCP contract analogous to the claude --mcp-config path is feasible. This is the ROADMAP reverse-direction slice.

An expired requester session permanently strands an unlaunched requested delegation: the expired session cannot heartbeat or be revived with the same session_id, while a fresh session is rejected from cancelled/needs_operator transitions as non-requester. Reproduced with zero attempts and no child sessions on the Fable and Opus review delegations.

Grok builder remains unqualified after successful fixed preflight and initialization. Investigate Grok terminal-tool interaction before another qualification attempt; process completion is not success.

Panel restart after the wave-3 merge was refused with project_state_binding_conflict ('Project state binding changed.'): the project registry (~/.config/agent-commons/projects/registry.json) pins the state root as device:inode 16777234:62607139, but after a reboot the same directory reports 16777230:62607139 (inode unchanged, device number changed). The check in ui/project_registry.py treats a device-number change as a binding conflict, so the multi-project panel cannot start until the registry is repaired; the coordinator started the 8787 panel with --single-project instead. Suggest a stable identity (inode plus a stored marker file/uuid, or re-binding when only the device number differs) and a documented repair command.

Operator-installed agent-commons CLI builds can lag lifecycle remediations that already validated newer canonical events: the pre-remediation uv-tool build replayed evt.01KY3202SBGJ9PCCHNWGRW5PNE under the old verification-authority rule, turning a valid reviewer verification into a doctor integrity failure and a falsely stale review.51GGP0F2TW6BR1EYP8HPBBBHBE, which blocked task acceptance. After any lifecycle-rule change is submitted, reinstall the operator CLI from the exact reviewed source (verify the registered manifest bytes first) before judging doctor failures or acting on projection staleness; the same stale-installed-build hazard was previously seen for the MCP runtime in review.1Z5YB8SH9XX3JRRW6AZXCHJX3K.

claude-independent-reviewer delegation requires a pre-existing open review request for the exact target, otherwise the child completes analysis but cannot record it and exits input_needed -> needs_operator, consuming the attempt and its provider budget. Evidence 2026-07-23, pilot-site workspace: delegation.6TR2GVQG4ZHM7HT30HDMSN1HMJ reported input_needed with sanitized verdict 'approved - all 4 acceptance criteria pass' because no review record existed for the target task; a rerun after review request creation (review.37AYGEABZ1W23B5635RP0VBC9E) recorded the review. delegation create should fail fast when purpose independent_review has no open review request matching the target ref and revision.

AGENTS.md's blanket PID rule does not match the test tree. It says tests must not hardcode pids, yet tests/runtime/test_attempts.py hardcodes pid=123 in ProcessResult/transition fixtures and tests/runtime/test_preflight.py does likewise. The real liveness-sensitive reconcile test correctly spawns and reaps a child via _dead_pid(), so the safe invariant appears narrower: never assume a hardcoded PID is dead/free. Rewrite the standard to that precise invariant or remove the literal PIDs so every stated rule matches repository reality.

The green contract omits frontend/work and frontend/gallery Node behavior suites and Gallery bundle parity. Makefile and .github/workflows/ci.yml do not execute the Gallery frontend tests; Work has a checked-in bundle freshness test but Gallery has no equivalent. A green make check therefore does not prove both modular frontends are source-parity and behavior-tested.

The bounded output budget is shared between stdout and stderr, so a provider that floods stderr can exhaust it before the answer arrives on stdout, and the truncation path added in e3b8ab9 will then close a held stdin while the reply is still missing. _BoundedOutput keeps a single _remaining counter across both channels (src/agent_commons/runtime/subprocess_runner.py, consume() decrements the same _remaining for whichever channel wrote), and e3b8ab9 closes held stdin as soon as output.truncated is true. The reasoning behind that change is correct — once the budget is gone the retained stdout is frozen, so a predicate that has not fired never will — but it assumes stdout is what consumed the budget. If stderr consumed it instead, the handshake probe closes stdin with an incomplete stdout and reproduces the race that bf482fd fixed, from a different cause. The diagnostic is then actively misleading rather than merely opaque: preflight reports outcome succeeded and reason completed, which is true of the process and hides that we cut it off. Not reproduced: with --ignore-user-config the Codex child is quiet and the handshake budget is 256 KiB, so this is a latent edge rather than an observed failure, and it was deliberately not fixed without evidence. If a preflight diagnosis ever points at an exhausted budget, the first question is which channel consumed it; a per-channel counter, or naming the channel in the diagnostic, would answer it.

Codex workspace-write sandbox blocks all canonical CLI writes because every canonical write acquires locks under .git/agent-commons-state (canonical-write.lock, sessions/registry.lock, idempotency-v2), and codex sandbox denies .git writes. A manual headless codex reviewer therefore cannot even register a session; only an interactive trusted codex window (or a future MCP path per the codex-wiring finding, since MCP servers run outside the child sandbox) can write canonically. Evidence 2026-07-23 pilot-site: headless codex reviewer refused verdict with 'sandbox blocks writes to .git/agent-commons-state/sessions/registry.lock'. Longer-term question (ADR-worthy): whether checkout-scoped state belongs under .git at all.

Ephemeral workers cannot write the task lifecycle at all: the tools do not exist, so the registry is a read-only bulletin board for the actors who do the work, and every downstream symptom follows from that. Measured on this ledger: broker-launched child sessions have produced 35 events in the whole history, and every one is instantaneous and terminal — 15 delegation.succeeded, 10 review.completed, 5 thread.replied, 3 delegation.needs_operator, 2 verification.recorded. Not one task.taken, task.started, task.completed, claim acquisition or artifact registration. Human and coordinator sessions wrote the full lifecycle over the same period: 67 taken, 71 started, 70 completed, 50 submitted, 30 accepted, 111 artifacts registered. The cause is not behaviour: grep across src finds zero occurrences of commons_take_task, commons_start_task, commons_complete_task, commons_submit_task, commons_register_artifact and commons_acquire_claim. The worker MCP scope exposes commons_list_tasks read-only alongside the terminal commons_succeed_delegation and commons_delegation_needs_operator. The workers did not bypass the lifecycle; it was never built for them. This reframes the six audit task records that stood in ready while their deliverables were committed: they were untakeable by construction, and closing them as reconciliation treated a structural gap as bookkeeping. It also explains the stale critical finding differently than assumed: the work that invalidated it was never obliged to touch the record, because the record is not the source of work. Consequence to design against, not merely to fix: with the registry optional for the actors who change the world, an absent record is cheaper than a wrong one, and the system drifts toward an audit trail that is honest and empty. The correction is to make the registry issue work rather than mirror it — the broker already knows the target task, creates the child session and binds the delegation, so it can record the take itself at the moment the fact is true.

Canonical records do not close themselves and nothing re-checks them, so the ledger drifts toward false alarm and false idleness, and the drift already changed planning. Two demonstrations from one day. First, finding.5MER0TQVSQ1Q2A2627WB0B1X3F sat critical and reported for about two weeks after the code that fixed it landed: commit 69262fb Add safe state ownership and task controls is dated 2026-08-07 and was in main long before, yet the finding was still treated as a live blocker and was written as a hard dependency into accepted decision.2VGMQ28H6NJ8FT779CE03RXVSV, which blocks the project sidebar. Work was planned around a defect that no longer existed; the eventual fix commit only added the regression test that proved it. Second, six audit task records stood in ready while their deliverables were committed under docs/audits/2026-08-18-code-quality/ in b2fe8d3 and 49c7b0d, and all six carried an empty work_author_session_ids, meaning no session ever took them and the lifecycle was bypassed entirely rather than left half-finished. Those six were closed as reconciliation rather than advanced through take and complete, because taking them now would bind them to a session that did not do the work and put a false author into append-only history. The cost is specific and asymmetric: a stale open critical finding stops work that could proceed, and a stale ready task hides work that is already done, so the record misleads in both directions at once. What is missing is not a state machine but a habit with a mechanism: nothing prompts a re-check of an open finding when related code lands, and nothing notices a task whose deliverable exists in the tree while its record never left ready. A product whose whole claim is who decided, who checked and who signed off cannot let its own record be the least current thing in the repository.

Adopt one governing rule for how the record stays current, and four mechanisms that follow from it. The rule: an obligation performed by the system at the moment the fact is true cannot be faked, while an obligation performed by an agent after the fact always can. Issuing a task is the first kind; asking a worker to close a record at the end of its session is the second, and it is therefore not adopted. Silence stays free, assertion is paid, and the price equals how much of other peoples freedom the assertion takes: writing nothing costs nothing, writing an observation costs nothing because it takes nothing from anyone, and writing a record that stops other work must carry an executable way to refute itself. Refusing to pay is allowed — the record lives, is visible and is read, but does not block. Four mechanisms, in order. First, the registry issues work rather than mirroring it: the broker already resolves the target task, creates the child session and binds the delegation, so it records the take itself at the moment the fact is true, which removes the fabricated-authorship problem instead of policing it. Second, verification happens on read rather than on write: the tool that returns a record returns it with the fresh result of its predicate and the age of its last confirmation, so revision is a by-product of use, priced to whoever benefits and proportional to the harm the record causes; a read path must not return a live blocker while its predicate is green. Third, a predicate earns authority only by demonstrating discriminating power across two revisions, red before the fix and green after: a bad predicate can be written but a tautologically green check cannot be made to turn red on the old code, so cheap compliance is rejected arithmetically rather than by judgement, and the predicate lives as a repository artifact whose weakening is a diff with an author. Fourth, automation may refute but never confirm: a green reproduction retires the evidence for a defect and removes its right to block, it does not declare the defect fixed, and closure remains a human act; automation may demote a divergence but never erase it, because divergence is data about the process and hiding it is a new kind of blindness. Two supporting positions. A projection over the ledger is required alongside read-time checking rather than instead of it, because once observers write contesting claims some rule must resolve them deterministically and make automatic actions reversible; read-time checking supplies freshness, the projection supplies resolvability. And the state vocabulary must be able to express result present, originator not established, because a schema that cannot state that truth forces a choice between a lie and silence and always receives silence.

The panel carries no capability gates: --enable-writes, --enable-catalog-editing and --enable-launch are all removed, and the fact that this software starts processes against the users paid provider subscription moves into the service description and the documentation instead of a flag typed at startup. The owners reasoning is that the flag was never evidence of anything: a person arriving at Codex is not asked to confirm that limits will be spent in each window, because that follows from what the service is, and a ceremony that everyone performs mechanically protects nobody. Launch routes register on every writable panel and refuse with launch_not_configured until the runtime environment is configured, because the first-run screen now configures it inside an already running panel and the route table is not rebuilt after startup. This supersedes the narrower decision that kept the launch flag as a deliberate act of consent; it does not claim the broker is ready — see the same-day replacement in scope broker-release-readiness, which carries the evidence gate forward untouched.

The panel gains a project list: create, open, close and reopen projects from the left sidebar, each project being one workspace with its own board. Two constraints are part of this decision. First, a project is not a session: sessions carry a TTL and an ownership nonce, so the panel holds and renews a session per open project rather than equating the two, otherwise a project left open past the TTL dies on its own and the audit trail suffers. Second, closing a project means closing its session and stopping the watch, never silently killing a live delegation — the runtime cannot reattach to an exited provider, so closing a project with a run in flight must be refused or explicitly confirmed. This makes one process serve N workspaces, which ADR 0005 currently governs and which finding.5MER0TQVSQ1Q2A2627WB0B1X3F reports as a critical open defect: the ambient exact operational state root is accepted across workspaces before ownership validation. That finding must be closed before the sidebar ships, because the sidebar turns the dangerous configuration into the normal operating mode.

Measure record health by what the record is silent about, not by what it contains. Primary: the share of repository changes not linked to any record, split by the cost of the change, watching whether it rises faster on expensive work such as migrations, data and security. It measures the share of the world the journal says nothing about, it can only be improved by genuinely linking work to records, and it deviates before a parallel private list appears, because that list is already a consequence of the broken link rather than its beginning. Second: the gap between when the world changed and when the record about it was written, median and tail — a growing tail against a stable median reads as batch compliance writing. Third: the share of records that actually block someone and carry a predicate with a fresh result; the remainder are unfalsifiable blockers and are the risk surface. Fourth, as an alarm rather than a success measure: the share of records closed by observation rather than by an executor claim, whose growth means work is migrating away from the lifecycle. Explicitly retired: the share of records confirmed within N days and the share of closed records, both of which are improved by a mass closing session. Also retired before adoption: the share of reads followed by independent verification in the source — it is sound today but the read-time checking mechanism above destroys it by construction, since the tool verifies on the readers behalf and the metric stops distinguishing trust from delegation of the check; it must be dropped in the same change that introduces read-time verification, not left to report a false green.

Performance baseline (300-task fixture, lock/read/replay/append split) is measured before fixing p50/p95 targets; 2 s and 8 s are temporary UI hint thresholds for "large project" and "no need to click again".

The CLI is frozen: security fixes only, no behaviour changes, no new features. MCP is untouched, because it is the brokers channel to worker processes rather than a user surface, and freezing it would stop delegation working at all. The freeze has a precondition that must not be skipped, because today the CLI is the only way to initialise a workspace and to open and carry a session: freezing it before the panel can do both would leave a new user unable to start the product at all. The freeze therefore takes effect per capability, not as a flag day — a CLI command may be frozen once the panel covers what it does, and the bootstrap commands stay live until the panel owns workspace initialisation and session lifecycle. Recorded consequence: the audit decision to skip decomposing cli.py stands and hardens, since polishing the structure of a surface under freeze is spent work.

UX closure packages run sequentially in this checkout (one writable worker), 60 minutes per run, launched per wave without per-run confirmation; Terra = codex-builder with model gpt-5.6-terra (qualified 2026-09-09 via profiles-terra.yaml), Opus = claude-builder, Grok = grok-builder; Astra (default Codex) and the Claude Fable coordinator review; formal independent reviews run through the broker with cross-provider reviewers. Executor mapping follows strengths: Opus frontend/design, Grok volume/mechanical/perf, Terra backend/domain/integration.

For authenticated Design Gallery preview, allow only public and internal PNG/JPEG artifacts. Always refuse restricted, pii and secret classifications; preview remains current-revision-only and uses verified server-side reads.
docs/archive/{plans,reviews} is the location of completed or superseded documents: moved byte-for-byte with a status stamp; historical is never only a label in prose (D-15).

The broker stays experimental and its evidence gate is unchanged: behavioral canaries green on macOS and Linux, 100 consecutive hermetic provider runs per supported provider without mismatch, and 20 real local launches with zero process_canonical_mismatch events. None of those conditions has been met and this decision does not claim otherwise. What changes is only how the experimental status is signalled to a person: it stops being a flag the operator types at startup and becomes a statement in the service description and the documentation, because the UI is now the primary surface and a startup flag is unreachable from it. The release stage label therefore reads experimental rather than experimental_manual_opt_in, which is a truthful narrowing — the software is no less experimental, the manual ceremony is simply gone. Recorded consequence: nothing here permits calling the broker ready, and the gate above remains the only thing that can.

docs/visual_multi_agent_orchestrator_prd.md and docs/visual_orchestrator_plan.md are rewritten in place to match the new course, rather than being left in force or merely marked historical. They currently carry eleven positions that contradict the pivot, including the visual layer as an optional overlay, profiles created outside the UI, and a mitigation against rewriting core for UI requirements. Leaving them would let a reader or an agent open them tomorrow and receive the opposite instructions. The rewrite is roughly two thousand lines of work and it does erase the trail of how the earlier positions were reached, which is acceptable only because that trail now lives in the ledger: each superseded position has a decision entry with its evidence and its rejected alternative. The rewrite must therefore cite those decision identifiers rather than restate conclusions, and anything not backed by a recorded decision must not silently change meaning during the rewrite.

Work opens on a "Now" view with three columns (Needs you / In progress / Up next) derived from existing attention/active/ready filters; the dependency graph moves to a "Map" tab and the full list to "All tasks". Navigation state stays allowlisted URL state, not canonical.

D-20 (owner, 2026-09-21): open source in about three months; a commercial licence for corporations or a sale may follow. Licence Apache-2.0 plus CLA/DCO from the first day so relicensing stays possible.
Phase 3 keeps the dark scheme (direction A): semantic CSS tokens replacing raw hex, 4n spacing and type scale, Card/StatusChip/Stepper/DecisionCard primitives. No light theme in scope.

A project opens on its board (ADR 0020, decision.47ZN20DCVTVP6HR2JB1MCV1V7W): standing roles as nodes, agent links as edges, departments as board frames. Codex workers receive one required agent-commons stdio MCP server through repeated exec-scoped -c mcp_servers.agent-commons.* overrides; command, args, and enabled_tools use generated TOML-compatible literals; --ignore-user-config and --strict-config exclude ambient user MCP and reject drift. Codex enabled_tools derive from the same purpose-specific raw worker catalog as Claude allowed-tools, the MCP child inherits AGENT_COMMONS_SESSION_ID, and local stdio MCP is treated as host-launched outside the model command sandbox. The paid compatibility canary becomes provider-generic with an explicit codex-independent-reviewer entry point.

Provider subscription state stays the user responsibility, documented as part of what the service is, and the product reports the provider failure honestly rather than pre-verifying it. Three states cannot be detected before a paid run: no subscription, model unavailable on the current plan, and exhausted limits. All three surface only when the provider talks to the model, which is after the process started and the attempt is committed; verifying them in advance would require a real billable call, so preflight cannot cover them by construction. Preflight stays credential-free and structural: missing executable, invalid config, MCP handshake. The runtime side is already largely satisfied by the bounded stderr tail added in P0-2, which puts the provider own error text in delegation show and in the panel. Remaining work is limited to documenting the boundary in the service description and confirming the stored stderr tail is visible at the moment a run fails in the panel, not only through delegation show.

agent_commons.evals stays a public surface. docs/evals/README.md documents it as a versioned catalogue carrying the version 2026-08-wave4-v1, and a documented versioned artifact behaves as public whether or not pyproject singles it out. Only the internal consumer moves into tests; the package is neither deleted nor hidden and needs no deprecation window. This is audit item V5, which the audit run already honoured in practice — the package was kept — but which never reached the ledger.

The UI becomes the primary surface of the product: a user installs from GitHub, runs it locally, and does the whole job in the panel rather than calling heterogeneous agents from a Codex window. This is a change of intent that must be reconciled with the existing visual orchestrator documents, which record the opposite premise: docs/visual_orchestrator_plan.md keeps the visual layer as an optional overlay and carries an explicit mitigation against rewriting core to satisfy UI requirements. Both positions cannot stand; this decision records the new intent and requires that the prior documents be superseded rather than silently contradicted. Scope note: the product stays local and single-user, so no accounts are implied — an earlier claim that UI-only requires user accounts was raised and withdrawn during the session.

CLI ceases to be the product centre and becomes a legacy compatibility, bootstrap and emergency/recovery adapter. Normal human product workflows migrate to the UI; MCP remains a purpose-scoped agent interface; unattended operator automation gains a typed service/Python boundary after the A8 thematic seams are complete. New product capabilities must land in thematic domain/service modules and be exposed through UI/MCP adapters, not new CLI command behaviour. The existing cli/_shared.py and cli/workspace.py split is grandfathered solely for still-live bootstrap support. No further CLI decomposition, new commands, behavioural changes, or removal occur without a separate owner-authorised bounded migration decision and explicit compatibility/recovery evidence.

Owner decision 2026-09-11: ADR 0021 (docs/adr/0021-objective-blueprint-application-provenance.md) is accepted as written after two independent reviews; WP-11.2 (canonical objective_id on tasks, immutable blueprint_application record, revision-bound manual join, additive tracker DTO fields) is implemented by Terra now, before wave 3.

Hiring a role happens entirely in the UI: the user picks provider family, concrete model, role name, then permissions, skills and system prompt. The product discovers provider executables itself on first run and generates the runtime configuration; the operator no longer hand-writes runtime.yaml to get a usable profile list. What stays outside the UI is the security-bearing part: which executable runs and under which sandbox mode. Evidence for the current break: with no runtime.yaml the profile select is empty and hiring cannot proceed, and the field format is undocumented — it was learned during the session by trial and error from ConfigurationError messages ("codex-builder has unsupported fields: permission_mode", "independent Claude reviewer must use dontAsk with fixed allowed tools"). This contradicts the recorded position that profiles are created outside the UI, which the panel also prints to the user; that position must be superseded, not quietly ignored.

For a local single-user product the three panel gates (--enable-writes, --enable-catalog-editing, --enable-launch) stop being process flags: the user who starts the product gets the whole product. The acknowledgement they used to carry — that this software starts paid processes on the user subscription — moves into the service description and a first-run notice. This decision conflicts with accepted decision.7PAPYKR4QRC018E372AF952ZZ9, which keeps the broker at experimental manual opt-in until an evidence gate is met, and it cannot simply override it: either the evidence gate is declared met and that decision is superseded, or the gates stay until it is. This entry records the intent and the conflict; it must not be implemented before that reconciliation.

Run and check-run time limits come from an additive real wall_time_seconds in DTOs ("limit not provided" when absent), and the user can change the run time limit in the Prepare run form within server-enforced bounds; the client is never trusted for the limit.

Retire the legacy single-file panel src/agent_commons/ui/static/index.html: ADR 0022 redirects / to /work, removes the asset, read_spa and its 16 tests, and retires the single-writer rule for that file from AGENTS.md and docs/FRONTEND_CONTRACT.md (D-12).

D-21 (owner, 2026-09-21): local-first is absolute. The task tracker stays in the app; Linear/Jira integration and export are not built. Trigger to revisit: a second real user who lives in an external tracker.

Built-in catalog content stays bilingual EN/RU. User-authored content (custom blueprints, skill groups, tasks) is entered once in the language the user typed and shown as-is under both UI locales; it is never translated and no second locale field is required.

Re-scope A6 from reducing full passes over a large ledger to removing the fixed floor of a single replay, and demote pass reduction to secondary. Measured on the heaviest real ledger available, this repository own workspace: 892 events over five weeks (14 July to 19 August), 3.7 MB, growing at roughly 500 to 650 events per month under daily dogfooding; a one-day customer project produced 69. A snapshot replay of that ledger costs 2.281, 2.322 and 2.341 seconds on three consecutive in-process calls, against 0.113 for package import and 0.151 for the manager constructor, so start-up is not the cost and the result is not cached between calls. Compared with the A0 baseline of 5.236654 seconds median at 20 000 events, a 22-fold increase in volume yields a 2.3-fold increase in time, which places roughly two seconds of fixed cost inside replay itself, largely independent of ledger size. The 20 000-event benchmark therefore represents about three years of the heaviest observed usage, and pass reduction optimises a case no user reaches. The floor is also what multi-project multiplies: N open projects pay it per change wave, not the growth of any one ledger, so this re-scope is a prerequisite for the project sidebar rather than an unrelated performance task. Before changing code, profile to confirm where the floor sits; audit finding E2 reports that verified SQLite reads deserialize every indexed document before replay, which is the first candidate. Note the two measurements may exercise different paths, so the profile is a required step and not a formality.

Keep the broker experimental and manual opt-in until an evidence gate passes: behavioral canaries are green on macOS and Linux, 100 consecutive hermetic provider runs per supported provider complete without mismatch, and 20 real local launches complete with zero process_canonical_mismatch events.
Use Dmitrii Ershov as the copyright holder in Apache-2.0 project notices. Use BejeweledMe only as the GitHub identity and project URL owner.

The move to React Flow is incremental, screen by screen, not a single rewrite. The new stack lives beside the existing asset and screens migrate one at a time, so the product keeps working throughout and there is never a window where it does not. This constrains the accepted frontend stack decision decision.33ZP85QCM4G48YWT79VFQM9E62 in three ways that must hold from the first migrated screen rather than being retrofitted. The two surfaces coexist, so the two-language string table and the vocabulary glossary need one shared source both consume, not a copy per stack, or they drift within a release. Packaging must serve both at once while the migration runs, and clone-and-run must keep working without a manual npm step throughout, not only at the end. The contract tests that enforce the frontend laws today have to keep passing for whatever has not moved yet, so docs/FRONTEND_CONTRACT.md is amended per screen rather than replaced in one go. The single-writer claim on the existing asset stays meaningful until the last screen leaves it.
